samir: FYI we saw a ~2.3x p99 jump during the midday ramp on canary. Not obvious from CPU/GPU metrics. Posting quick profiling results.
maya: Ugh. Same window as the customer burst tests?
samir: Yup. Short spike (~45s) after throughput doubled. p50 unchanged, p95 +15%, p99 +130%.
sasha: Any kernel selector fallbacks in logs? Could be switching to slower matmul due to sequence length mismatch.
samir: Checked. Kernel selector stayed on 'fused-attn-v1' mostly, but there were a handful of fallback runs to 'matmul-gemm' during the spike. Logs:
```
[11:04:12] kernel_choice: fused-attn-v1
[11:04:12] fallback: matmul-gemm (latency_penalty_ms=48)
[11:04:13] kv_cache_miss:true
```
liam: kv_cache_miss:true looks suspicious — maybe cold KV pages from preempted worker? Did autoscaler evict pods during ramp?
samir: Autoscaler did one scale-up, new pods came up without warmed KV. Scale-up lag ~22s, then we hit sustained high qps. New replicas were accepting traffic while still populating KV.
eva: So tail is 1) fallback kernel penalty, 2) KV cold-miss on new replicas, 3) microbatching behavior during the instant ramp.
sasha: What microbatch policy were we using for that canary? static microbatch cap 8 with aggressive batching window (20ms).
maya: Right — that combo is great for throughput, but when a bunch of cold replicas join, we get larger aggregated batch sizes hitting cold KV and a few fallbacks. The queueing then amplifies p99.
liam: I pushed a small experiment: lower microbatch_cap -> 2 and add a short ramp grace (hold-new-replicas for 10s with warm-up routing) to test.
samir: Ran 3 runs. Summary:
```
config A (cap=8, no grace): p99=420ms, kv-cold-events=17, fallback=12
config B (cap=2, grace=10s): p99=210ms, kv-cold-events=3, fallback=1
config C (adaptive cap based on inflight<50 -> cap=8 else cap=2): p99=230ms, kv-cold-events=4
```
sasha: Nice. So adaptive cap + warm grace seems promising. Did you profile kernel selector thresholds? Could we bias to avoid fallback if seq_len distribution spikes?
samir: Yes — kernel selector threshold was purely perf-model based; we can add a hysteresis: prefer the faster fused-attn unless fallback delta > 2x and keep pinned for 50ms. That reduced flip-flop on selector in the tests.
eva: Can we avoid targeting new replicas with full traffic until KV warmed? Maybe a cheap prewarm RPC that touches a sample of keys before marking ready.
liam: We can do soft-preheat: route 10% traffic to new pods while they warm; or run a background kv-populate on creation.
maya: Both are doable. Background prepopulate needs to be careful about rate limiting and cost.
samir: Also noticed that the quantized kernel regressed slightly for certain seq lengths — increased kernel latency variance. We'll add histogram monitoring per-kernel per-seqlen (p50/p95/p99).
sasha: Good call. Monitoring will help detect regressions earlier. Also add a metric for 'kv_miss_rate_on_first_minute'
deploy-bot: [deploy] rolled canary experiment 1998765400 -> 1998765460: config B applied to 10% of traffic
samir: After canary B roll, p99 stabilized ~220ms and no customer-reported issues. Next steps:
- prod experiment: enable soft-preheat + adaptive microbatch for 5% traffic tomorrow morning
- add selector hysteresis and per-kernel histograms
- add kv-warm metric and dashboard
maya: I'll file a postmortem-lite doc with the runbook changes and link the configs.
liam: I'll prototype the prewarm RPC and the adaptive cap controller.
eva: I'll own the monitoring dashboards and set a p99 alert threshold for new-replica cold hits.
samir: Thanks team. Short action items and clear wins. :thumbsup:
